context_subtitle: This section is optional and fully anonymous. Your answers here do not affect the calculation of your N distribution — they're only used to characterize the sample of participants and for supplementary research purposes. Leave any item blank if you'd rather not answer.
context_official_classification_note: We use CNPq's official area classification; terms are shown in Portuguese, the official nomenclature in Brazil. In presentations, results will be aggregated only by broad field.
context_beliefs_section_title: Your beliefs about life in the universe
ctx_q_life_solar: Do you think any form of life exists (or existed) elsewhere in the Solar System, besides Earth?
ctx_q_life_galaxy: Do you think any form of life currently exists elsewhere in the Milky Way, besides Earth?
ctx_q_intel_galaxy: Do you think detectable intelligent life currently exists elsewhere in the Milky Way?
ctx_q_life_universe: Do you think any form of life currently exists elsewhere in the observable universe, beyond the Milky Way?
ctx_q_intel_universe: Do you think detectable intelligent life currently exists elsewhere in the observable universe?
Ns_param: Number of stars in the galaxy
Ns_question: How many stars are there in the Milky Way?
fp_question: What fraction of stars form planets?
ne_param: number of habitable planets per star
ne_question: What is the average number of habitable planets per star?
fl_question: On what fraction of habitable planets does any form of life emerge?
fi_param: fraction of habitable planets with life that develop intelligence
fi_question: On what fraction of habitable planets with life does intelligence evolve?
fc_question: What fraction of planets with intelligent life are capable of interstellar communication?
fL_param: Fraction of stellar lifetime with detectable civilization
fL_question: What fraction of a star's lifetime is an extraterrestrial technological civilization on one of its planets detectable?
slider_hint: The peak is your most likely value. The side handles set your uncertainty on each side.
skip_btn: Skip. I do not have enough knowledge to estimate this parameter.
skip_warning_title: Skipping this question prevents calculation of your N.
skip_warning_body: All parameters are required to compute the estimated number of detectable civilisations. You may continue, but your personal N distribution will not be shown at the end.
skipped_badge: This question is skipped — your N distribution will not be calculated.
interaction_warning: Move the slider at least a little or skip this question.
intro_eq_body: In 1961, Frank Drake proposed an equation to estimate the number of detectable extraterrestrial technological civilizations in the Milky Way. It multiplies seven parameters, each representing a step on the path from star formation to interstellar communication. Variations of those parameters are often used. Here, we will use the Carl Sagan's version, that starts with the number of stars in the Milky Way.
intro_eq_note: N = number of extraterrestrial detectable civilizations in the Milky Way today
intro_why_body: The values of the parameters are deeply uncertain and depend on very different areas of knowledge — astrophysics, biology, cognitive sciences. This survey seeks to capture the beliefs and uncertainties of the Brazilian astrobiological community in a quantitative way.
intro_step1: For each parameter, you will move a slider that defines a probability distribution — not a single value, but the range of values you consider plausible and how likely each one is.
intro_step2: At the end, your personal distribution of N will be calculated and you can see how it compares to that of the community.
intro_step3: You can return later to view the aggregated results as more participants respond.
intro_demo_caption: Drag the centre handle (■) to move the peak and the side handles (○) to adjust uncertainty.
consent_what_body: This survey is conducted by Fernando Mello with the aim of quantifying the beliefs and uncertainties of experts about the parameters of the Drake Equation. The data will be used exclusively for academic purposes.
consent_data_1: Your probability distributions for each parameter of the Drake Equation
consent_data_2: Answers to supplementary questions about beliefs in intelligent extraterrestrial life
consent_data_4: No personally identifiable information is required
consent_rights_1: Voluntary participation — you may stop and withdraw from the survey at any time before submission
consent_rights_2: Data is anonymous and aggregated — as we do not collect your identity, responses cannot be modified or deleted after submission
consent_rights_3: Confidentiality guarantee — your responses will be analyzed in aggregate and never individually, preventing your identification
consent_rights_4: Contact and transparency — you have the right to ask the researcher questions and access the study's final results
consent_chk1: I have read and understood the information above about this research.
consent_chk2: I voluntarily consent to participate and I know that I can withdraw my consent at any time.
consent_chk3: I authorize the use of my data in an anonymous and aggregated form for scientific research purposes.
results_subtitle: Based on your distributions, we calculated your personal estimate of N — the number of detectable civilizations in the Milky Way today.
results_mc_note: Distribution calculated by Monte Carlo simulation (20,000 samples)
